title: auth-api-401-429-debug-scratchpad-followup
content:
Purpose:
Follow-up scratchpad from initial notes (auth-api-401-429-debug-scratchpad). Collecting extra breadcrumbs after mitigation steps. Keep rough.

Short summary update:
- Rotated keys for org-alpha reduced 401 volume but not eliminated. 401s still sporadic for org-beta.
- CI job change (scoped to sandbox) reduced many 429 spikes; however org-level buckets still show exhaustion during abnormal windows.
- Router config review flagged a potential bucket-hash collision for org ids with similar prefixes after 2026-03-02 deploy.

New timeline notes:
- 2026-03-05 02:14 UTC: Michael ran router simulation locally with traffic mix and reproduced double-counting for ~5% of requests when service accounts have missing org header.
- 2026-03-05 09:40 UTC: Ran targeted test sending explicit X-Org-ID header and trace-id -> router attributed correctly. When header missing, router fell back to api_key->org mapping; in a small window mapping table lookup returned stale mapping for key 'key-789' (cached value).
- 2026-03-05 11:05 UTC: Added temporary debug flag to router to log resolved_org for 1 minute for keys in affected org list (org-alpha, org-beta). Collected 1200 lines.

Commands / reproducer tried since last note:
- encoding tests (python vs curl):
  * python requests example that used auth header via requests.Session.headers['Authorization'] -> no failure locally.
  * python requests example where header passed in third-party wrapper that URL-encodes values -> reproduced invalid_signature. Wrapper encoded '+' as space when signing canonical string.
- router attribution test: small loop with/without X-Org-ID to see bucket assignment
  for i in $(seq 1 200); do \
    curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -H "X-Trace-ID: t-$i" -H "X-Org-ID: org-beta" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" &
    sleep 0.02
  done
  Observed consistent 200s and router logs showing bucket=org-beta. Removing X-Org-ID caused occasional bucket assignment to org-internal (bad).

Logs/trace excerpts (sanitized):
- router (2026-03-05T09:41:12Z) - trace_id=t-42 - resolved_org=org-internal - api_key_id=key-789 - reason=cache_miss_then_fallback
- auth (2026-03-05T09:41:12Z) - auth_result=authenticated - key_lookup=ok
- application (2026-03-05T09:41:12Z) - upstream_status=200

Observations from collected data:
- Router cache TTL for api_key->org mapping set to 30s in 2026-03-02 deploy; race seen when key rotation happens concurrently (cache invalidation not propagated) -> temporary mis-attribution.
- Encoding issue confirmed in one customer wrapper (plus->space) causing HMAC mismatch. This explains some invalid_signature events.
- Double-counting hypothesis seemed less likely after counting fixes; most 429s mapped to bucket exhaustion caused by missing X-Org-ID or mapping to internal org with a small shared bucket.

Hypotheses updated (ranked):
1) Router api_key->org cache TTL too short and invalidation race during rotations causing occasional mis-attribution to internal org buckets -> 429s for customers. (High confidence)
2) Customer-side wrapper encoding bug producing invalid_signature -> 401s for that customer's traffic. (Confirmed for one customer)
3) Edge middleware rewriting Authorization for specific UA still possible but lower frequency. (Medium confidence)

Mitigations applied / proposed:
- Increased router cache TTL from 30s -> 300s as temporary mitigation (rolled 2026-03-05T13:00Z). Monitor for over-attribution; revert if stale mappings persist too long.
- Add explicit X-Org-ID check: if present, prefer header for bucket selection and log mismatch when header org != api_key org. (PR drafted: infra/PR-419)
- For customers using the buggy wrapper, CS sent guidance to update SDK usage. Added a chunk to support pages documenting correct header handling.
- Edge-auth PR (PR-412) merged to canonicalize Authorization header before signature check (normalizes + and space, percent-encoding). Deployed to canary 2026-03-05T14:20Z.

Data to collect next (remaining):
- Monitor 24h of org-per-minute bucket metrics for org-alpha and org-beta post cache-ttl change.
- Confirm no other customers use the buggy wrapper (search telemetry for signature_mismatch + user_agent patterns).
- Correlate billing webhook events for last 7 days to ensure quota changes were not missed.

Tests to run (next):
- Run chaos test: rotate a key while firing requests to ensure cache invalidation path doesn't mis-attribute (simulate rapid rotation + traffic).
- Run client-encoding matrix (curl, python-requests plain, python-requests via wrapper, node-fetch) against edge-auth canary and compare auth_result and error messages.

Owners / next actions:
- Lena: monitor post-deploy metrics and collect 24h bucket graphs (due 2026-03-07).
- Michael: push PR-419 to add header-precedence logic and merge after review. Also follow-up to make cache invalidation stronger (event-driven).
- Ravi: coordinate CS communication to affected customers and prepare KB article for header/SDK guidance.
- SRE: keep emergency lift plan available if customers see repeat exhaustion.

Notes / random items:
- Consider adding a more descriptive 401 error code for invalid_signature cases that includes a short fingerprint to help customers debug (not the key or secret, just a header hash). Need privacy review.
- Long-term: move to token introspection service that emits stable org_id for each request (single source of truth) rather than multiple caches across router nodes.

Slack/JIRA links: JIRA-INF-2387, infra/PR-412, infra/PR-419 (draft), slack:#infra-alerts thread CAJ92K3H2.

End of scratchpad follow-up.

-- Lena
